PostgreSQL: a foreign key rejects inserting a referencing row whose value matches no referenced row, and with the default action (NO ACTION) rejects deleting a referenced row that still has referencing rows.

claims.text: EF Core can send a SQL string through a DbContext's connection (e.g. Database.SqlQuery/FromSql); the compiler does not check table or column names in it, so a wrong name fails only when the query runs, with an error from the database.

git grep -n -e <p1> -e <p2> <tree> -- <pathspec>... searches the given tree (a tag) for lines matching any of the patterns, limited to the pathspecs, and prints path:line:text prefixed by the tree name. At stage-3 the Try it command prints exactly two lines.

A module owns a table when only its own code reads and writes it; C# queries are stopped by the mapping and internal, SQL strings only by people (e.g. code review), so ownership needs no separate database or schema change.
A foreign key between two modules' tables can stay while they share one database and is a coupling to remove only before they move to separate databases.
A query that joins another module's tables makes the module sending it depend on that module's table and column names, which the contract exists to hide.
At stage-3 Ordering is DonHang.Domain plus DonHang.Infrastructure, and DonHangDbContext is its DbContext.
